sections.h2: How do I sell my house fast in Miami Beach?
sections.html:
Pick the route first: a listing, a private sale or a cash offer. A cash buyer shortens the timeline, a listing usually reaches more buyers, and Miami Beach adds local rental rules that can change what your house is worth to an investor.

The city has 7.69 square miles of land and 81,594 residents in the Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate. That is a 1.6 percent drop from the April 2020 estimates base, and 2010 counted 87,779 people, so the city has not been adding residents the way the rest of Miami-Dade has.

  • Single-family house: check the short-term rental ban before pricing it as an investment.
  • Condo or apartment unit: ask the association for its rental rules and any pending assessments.
  • Inherited or tenant-occupied property: expect extra steps before a deed can be signed.

sections.h2: What do Census figures show about Miami Beach homes?
sections.html:
Miami Beach has more owners than the city of Miami next door but still a majority of renters. QuickFacts lists a 40.9 percent owner-occupied rate and 41,600 households averaging 1.95 people for 2020 to 2024.

The Census also counts 18.8 percent of residents as 65 or older and a per capita income of $75,054, which helps explain why many sales here involve estates, downsizing and second homes.

Owners without a mortgage still carry a median monthly cost of $1,393, which is mostly taxes, insurance and fees. That is worth knowing if you are deciding whether to keep a vacant house.

sections.h2: Can I use my Miami Beach house as a short-term rental?
sections.html:
Not if it is a single-family home. The city's Resiliency Code (sections 7.5.4.13(d)(E) and 7.5.4.11(a)) prohibits vacation rentals of less than six months and one day in all single-family homes and in many multi-family buildings in certain zoning districts.

Permitted short-term rentals need a city Business Tax Receipt and a Resort Tax account, and city code section 102-386 requires both numbers to appear in every advertisement or listing. The city also publishes a list of apartment buildings authorized for short-term rental, with addresses grouped by zoning district.

A buyer who plans to operate a short-term rental will check all of this, and so should you. If your listing or past rental income assumed nightly stays that the code does not allow, expect a buyer to price the house as a long-term rental or owner-occupied home.

sections.h2: What costs and taxes apply when a Miami Beach house sells?
sections.html:
The deed stamp tax is the largest fixed item, and Miami-Dade County has its own rate. The Department of Revenue prints 60 cents per $100 plus a 45 cents per $100 surtax for the county, and the surtax is not due on a document transferring only a single-family dwelling.

Consideration for the tax includes money, a discharged obligation and any mortgage or encumbrance on the property, whether or not the buyer assumes it. The clerk collects the tax when the deed is recorded, and every party to the document is liable for it regardless of who agrees to pay.

  • Recording: $5.00 first page and $4.00 each additional page under section 28.24, plus added trust fund and technology charges.
  • Payoffs: mortgage, home equity line, judgment liens and any unpaid property tax.
  • Association items for condos and co-ops: ask for an estoppel or payoff letter early.

sections.h2: How do property tax dates affect a Miami Beach sale?
sections.html:
Florida values property as of January 1, mails proposed tax notices in August and sends bills in November. Bills paid in November carry a 4 percent discount, 3 percent in December, 2 percent in January and 1 percent in February, and unpaid bills become delinquent on April 1.

A homestead owner in Miami Beach who sells loses the exemption on that parcel, and the buyer's assessment resets to just value the next January 1. Miami-Dade's property appraiser handles exemptions, and the property appraiser's office states that it does not send bills; the county tax collector does.

The appraiser certified the 2026 roll on October 16, 2026. Ask the title company to prorate the year's tax at closing and to confirm whether the current bill is paid.

sections.h2: What should I know about older buildings and repairs?
sections.html:
Median owner costs and a median rent of $1,826 show that a Miami Beach property carries steady expenses even when it sits empty. The Census page does not list the age of the housing stock for this city, so ask your own inspector what the roof, plumbing and electrical system need.

Work done without a permit can surface during a sale. Ask the city building department whether permits on your parcel are open or closed, and give that answer to any buyer in writing. A cash buyer may accept a house with unfinished work, but the price will reflect it.

sections.h2: How do I compare a cash offer with listing in Miami Beach?
sections.html:
Start from the net you would keep after commission, repairs, carrying costs and the time on market, then compare it with the written cash figure. The cash offer should state who pays the stamp tax, title insurance and recording charges, and what happens to any deposit.

Ask for a closing date in writing and confirm that a title company or attorney will close. If the buyer wants the right to assign the contract, ask who the end buyer will be before you commit.

faqs.q: Is it legal to short-term rent a Miami Beach single-family house?
faqs.a: No. The city says short-term rentals of less than six months and one day are prohibited in all single-family homes. Condo and apartment rules depend on the zoning district and the building.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in Miami Beach?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau lists $556,700 for owner-occupied housing units for 2020 to 2024. That is a citywide midpoint, so your own house may be worth well above or below it.

faqs.q: Who pays the deed stamp tax on a Miami Beach sale?
faqs.a: Under the Department of Revenue's wording, all parties to the document are liable no matter who agrees to pay. Your contract decides who actually pays, so read that clause.

faqs.q: When do Florida property tax bills arrive?
faqs.a: The tax collector sends bills in November, and the discount is 4 percent for November payment. Unpaid taxes become delinquent on April 1.

faqs.q: Does my homestead cap go to the buyer?
faqs.a: No. A sale counts as a change of ownership, so the property goes back to just value the next January 1. You can ask the appraiser about portability for a new Florida homestead.
